headline: Ex-DMP chief and 2 cops sentenced to death over Rampura shootings
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has convicted former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman and two others for crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced former Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Habibur Rahman and two other police officials to death for crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising.
The other death-row convicts are former Khilgaon Zone Additional Deputy Commissioner Md Rashedul Islam and former Rampura Police Station chief Md Mashiur Rahman.

The tribunal also sentenced another police official to life imprisonment and a fifth to 20 years in prison. Only one convict, ASI Chanchal Chandra Sarkar, is currently in custody; the others are absconding.
The case involved three primary charges. The first concerned the indiscriminate firing by police on July 19, which resulted in the death of 38-year-old Md Nadeem.
The second charge involved the shooting of 18-year-old Amir Hossain, who was shot six times while hanging from a building's cornice to save his life.
The third charge detailed the death of 60-year-old Maya Islam and the attempted murder of her 6-year-old grandson, Basit Khan Musa, who was shot through the head by police fire.
The verdict was delivered by a three-member bench led by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder on Sunday.
caption:
Death sentences for an ex-DMP chief and two other police officials for crimes against humanity in Rampura.

The International Crimes Tribunal has sentenced former Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Commissioner Habibur Rahman and two other police officials to death for crimes against humanity during the 2024 July Uprising.

The other death-row convicts are former Khilgaon Zone Additional Deputy Commissioner Md Rashedul Islam and former Rampura Police Station chief Md Mashiur Rahman.

The tribunal also sentenced another police official to life imprisonment and a fifth to 20 years in prison. Only one convict, ASI Chanchal Chandra Sarkar, is currently in custody; the others are absconding.

The case involved three primary charges. The first concerned the indiscriminate firing by police on July 19, which resulted in the death of 38-year-old Md Nadeem.

The second charge involved the shooting of 18-year-old Amir Hossain, who was shot six times while hanging from a building's cornice to save his life.

The third charge detailed the death of 60-year-old Maya Islam and the attempted murder of her 6-year-old grandson, Basit Khan Musa, who was shot through the head by police fire.

The verdict was delivered by a three-member bench led by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder on Sunday.
